events.what: Baek and Balko prove ES(n)=2^(n-2)+1 for decomposable point sets (a class including Erdős–Szekeres cap/cup constructions and Horton-type sets)
Same paper: every set of 2^(k-2)+1 points in general position contains a split k-gon, tight
Bogdan reports UNSAT certificates for some anchored subfamilies toward ES(7)=33, without completing the case

judgement.doubts: Decomposable sets restrict the class of point sets quantified over, so this is a case of the bullet, not a variant, though the class is defined for the proof technique. The record never found an arXiv version of Baek–Balko; if one predates 26 January 2024 the event would be pre-snapshot and the status would fall to open. Bogdan's SAT work covers only some subfamilies of n=7 and is not movement.

corrections.why: F8: the status rests on the Baek–Balko decomposable-sets result; Bogdan's preprint 'explicitly reports only UNSAT certificates for some anchored subfamilies' (instances), so it cannot set the status and its author is not credited for it.

other: kept. Decomposable sets are a restriction of the point sets (case), in a peer-reviewed SoCG paper. One doubt: the record could not find an arXiv version, so a pre-snapshot first posting cannot be ruled out.
